subject.title: Compaction: use single-pass summarization when the summarizer's context window fits the whole history (skip forced map-reduce)

question: Should OpenClaw optimize compaction with an internal, conservative single-pass eligibility path for large-context summarizers, rather than add operator-facing chunk-ratio or parts configuration?
rationale: The report identifies a plausible performance improvement, but the acceptable trade-off between compaction speed, model/provider token-accounting variance, and a new public configuration surface is a product and reliability decision.

options.title: Sponsor conservative internal fast path
options.body: Prefer an automatic single-pass path guarded by conservative token and output reserves, with the existing split planner retained as fallback.

options.title: Add an advanced operator setting
options.body: Expose a narrowly documented opt-in only if model-specific limits cannot be represented safely by the existing planner inputs.

options.title: Keep current split behavior
options.body: Retain map-reduce as the universal policy if summary reliability across providers outweighs the reported latency gains.

recommendation.title: Sponsor conservative internal fast path
recommendation.body: Prefer an automatic single-pass path guarded by conservative token and output reserves, with the existing split planner retained as fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: The reporter has the only concrete affected deployment evidence currently available and can validate the resulting behavior, while code-area ownership still needs repository history review.
